answer: Resist sybils with proof of live serving capacity: each identity must run a public inference endpoint and answer surprise, unpredictable requests from peers within a tight deadline, proving it controls real, distinct compute. A crystal-clear ledger records each endpoint uptime and latency, and a meadow of independent provers cross-checks the answers against the same model. One server can pretend to be many names, but the delta between claimed identities and real serving capacity exposes the farm: each fake identity costs a full GPU worth of work, so scale itself becomes the price.
